title: Eager DNS invalidation on peering switchover to prevent stale cross-tenant responses
creator: Marco Hernandez
summary: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS anomalies after VPC peering failover: long-lived stale DNS replies were replayed to new tenant sessions following peering switchover, causing traffic to be misrouted and customer requests to fail authorization checks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two tenants A and B with peered dedicated VPCs and per-tenant DNS resolver. 2) Resolve service.example.internal from tenant A (positive A record cached at peering proxy). 3) Trigger peering switchover (simulate control-plane peering BGP/route failover or orchestrated peering replacement). 4) Immediately resolve same name from tenant B and observe stale A record returned by peering proxy. 5) Verify that client IP/SNAT mapping in logs shows tenant B but DNS response corresponds to tenant A backend.
investigation: Initial triage (03/10) showed the peering proxy maintains an in-process DNS answer cache keyed only by hostname and upstream view, not by tenant identifier. During rapid peering state changes the cache entries persisted and were delivered to the next flow before per-tenant conntrack/SNAT entries fully converged. Packet captures show identical DNS ID and answer body replayed across tenant flows. The proxy's cache TTL was honoring upstream TTL, but local state invalidation on peering-change was missing. We also observed race between peering controller (xchg) and dataplane flow reconciliation: flow table updates lag ~200-700ms during switchover which is enough for a cached DNS reply to be replayed.
root_cause: Design gap: DNS cache at the peering layer was keyed without tenant scoping and lacked proactive invalidation on peering topology changes. Operational gap: peering switchover does not emit a guaranteed synchronous cache-invalidate signal to all proxies.
mitigation: Short-term mitigation applied (03/11): 1) Deploy config to aggressively reduce local cache TTL to 0.25x for peered zones for affected regions; 2) Add peering-controller hook to send invalidation event to proxies in the same control-plane transaction; 3) Emergency customer-facing mitigation: added flow-level guard to block cached DNS answers if conntrack shows recent SNAT remap (<1s). These mitigations reduced customer error rate by ~92% in canary region.
permanent_fix_plan: Implement tenant-scoped cache keys (hostname + tenant_id + peering_epoch) in the peering proxy, and add an atomic peering-epoch bump on any topology change to force safe cache eviction across all proxies. Update peering-controller to publish peering_epoch and ensure proxies fetch epoch at connect time. This fix requires data-plane change (proxy) + control-plane update (peering-controller) + migration steps for rolling epoch bump.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flagged implementation behind 'tenant_scoped_dns_cache' flag. 2) Canary in us-west-2 on 10% of dedicated tenants with monitoring. 3) Gradual ramp by region over 48 hours. 4) If errors > 1% of baseline in canary, rollback to reduced-TTL mitigation. 5) Once stable, flip flag globally and remove aggressive TTL config after 72 hours.
test_plan: Unit tests for cache key generation, integration tests simulating peering switchover with tenant flows, synthetic chaos test to exercise peering-controller epoch bump, and end-to-end QA with two dedicated customers in staging to validate no leaked DNS answers across tenant boundaries.
monitoring_and_alerting: Added temporary SLO: DNS cross-tenant mismatch rate (count of DNS response where backend IP belongs to different tenant) threshold 0.1% for canary. Dashboards: peering-proxy cache hit/miss by tenant_id, peering_epoch drift, conntrack remap latency. Pager rule: page on >3 distinct tenants observing mismatches in 5 minutes.
